title: The titles tell the whole story.
detail: Read only the titles, in order. A reader must understand the point and follow the narrative without supporting copy or artwork.

title: Each title connects to the one before it.
detail: Name the subject clearly. Make the connection explicit when needed. Avoid vague fragments or pronouns whose meaning depends on hidden body copy.

title: Every slide advances one point.
detail: Use the number and types of slides the story needs. A problem, comparison, example, diagram or takeaway is a tool, not a mandatory sequence.

title: Details deepen the story.
detail: Supporting copy and illustrations can explain or substantiate a title. They must not supply a missing logical connection.

title: Substance comes from evidence.
detail: Source factual claims before publication. Label invented examples clearly and distinguish observations from advice or hypotheses.

title: Write the sequence before choosing layouts.
detail: Review the titles as one short paragraph first. Keep typography, spacing and branding consistent, while choosing color and illustration to suit the story.
